A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
these tobacco-derived DNA adducts are mutagenic and cytotoxic in human cells, and multiple TLS DNA polymerases are involved in the bypass of these lesions in human cells.
the POB adduct O4-POBs-dT is the most cytotoxic lesion, while O2-POBs-dTs and O6- POBs-dGs are less toxic.

The main takeaway from our work is that
these lesions, which are formed by tobacco-derived nitrosamine exposure, are cytotoxic, mutagenic, and can be bypassed by multiple TLS DNA polymerases in human cells.
the POB adduct O6-POBs-dG is a highly mutagenic lesion, whereas the POB addut O4-POBs-dT is a potent cytotoxic lesion.
POB adduct-induced DNA replication errors may be responsible, in part, for the mutagenic and carcinogenic properties of tobacco-specific nitrosoamines.
